experimentContext: Compare the anonymous DoorDash Commerce Platform storefront with the user's signed-in Uber Eats context for one overlapping scheduled pickup opportunity.
tipPolicy: Set optional pickup tips to $0 before recording a final checkout total.
comparisonStatus: Uber Eats was $1.19 cheaper than Bhatti's DoorDash-powered direct storefront for one equivalent basket. Its $1.20 signed-in membership benefit reversed the one-cent pre-benefit advantage of the direct checkout.
limitations: The restaurant was closed for immediate ordering. The direct pickup window was 12:40–12:50 PM and the Uber Eats window was 12:30–1:00 PM, producing a shared 12:40–12:50 PM opportunity.
This is one basket at one restaurant on one date, not evidence of a persistent cheapest channel.
The direct storefront was anonymous and Uber Eats was signed in because those were the user's normal available paths; account context is recorded per observation.

The direct checkout exposed optional sides, desserts, and drinks while Uber Eats exposed no modifiers for this item. Every optional direct add-on was left unselected, quantity remained one, and neither channel received a note.
The 183-second timer began after location and basket parity were established, so it measures basket assembly through immediate quote recheck rather than end-to-end restaurant discovery.
Both temporary carts were empty before assembly and were cleared within 282 seconds of the timed start. No order was placed.

observations.notes: The anonymous checkout showed pickup fulfillment, the scheduled window, a $0 tip, and the $26.07 total immediately before the final order action. No contact or payment information was entered.
